title: Keep the backlog sweep's vitest timeout clear of its CI wall time so a green tree stops timing out

source.ref: #4481 test job 2026-11-02: sweep case passed at 88,829ms against a 90,000ms timeout; #4482 re-run timed out at 90s on the same tree

detail:
The real-tree sweep case in backlog-contract.test.ts carried a 90s vitest timeout set when one full run took 20s. The list has since grown to 2,158 probes for 314s of CPU, which on the 4-core runner is about 80s of wall with nothing else running (HYG-184 already moved the file off the shared workers). On 2026-11-02 the sweep read 88.8s on CI (#4481, green by 1.2s) and timed out on the next PR (#4482) with nothing in that PR touching a probe's cost. The file's own doctrine (LIVE-047, ADR-1107) says wall time is not a property of any probe and the budget is CPU: guardCpuMs against BASE + allowance x n, which passed. So the wall clock had quietly become the gate. Fix: the sweep case's timeout goes to 360s, documented as a hang detector, with the CPU assertions untouched. The per-PR case stays at 90s (53s measured; HYG-184's probe pins that literal). The probe reads the sweep timeout and fails when it is under 2x the wall measured that day.

 Fixed 2026-11-02.
